voice.text: Every year, your birthday comes around again. [pause] What does Earth do, to make one whole year go by? Tap your guess.

Earth <emphasis>rotates</emphasis>. That means it spins, like a top. [pause] One full spin takes about twenty-four hours — one day and one night. The side facing the sun has day. The side facing away has night.

Earth also <emphasis>revolves</emphasis>. That means it travels, all the way around the sun. [pause] One full trip takes a whole year. [pause] Remember: rotate is spin. Revolve is travel. Two different words, two different motions.

Eight planets revolve around the sun, always in the same order. [pause] Mercury, scorched and swift. Venus, hottest, wrapped in thick clouds. Earth, our blue home. Mars, the rusty red planet. Jupiter, the biggest of all. Saturn, with its shining rings. Uranus, tipped over on its side. And Neptune — far, blue, and windy.
The four planets near the sun are small and rocky — you could stand on them. [pause] The four outer planets are gas giants: huge balls of gas, with no ground to stand on.

And the sun? The sun is not a planet. It is a <emphasis>star</emphasis> — and it is absurdly bigger than everything else. [pause] If the sun were a beach ball, Earth would be a tiny peppercorn. More than one million Earths could fit inside the sun.
One more secret. Posters squeeze the planets together, so they fit on the page. [pause] In real space, the planets are far, far apart — with huge stretches of empty space between them.
Build the solar system! Tap the planet that goes in the next spot, starting closest to the sun. [pause] If you get stuck, remember: My Very Educated Mother Just Served Us Noodles.
Rotate, or revolve? [pause] Rotate means spin. Revolve means travel around the sun. Tap the motion that matches each clue.
Last round! Think about real sizes, and real distances, in space.
All done, astronomer! [pause] Now show what you know.
Not quite. Use the memory trick: My Very Educated Mother Just Served Us Noodles.
Not quite. Remember: rotate is spin — it makes day and night. Revolve is travel — the trip around the sun makes a year.
Not quite. The sun is not just a bit bigger. It is absurdly bigger — over a million Earths would fit inside it.
Not quite. Posters squeeze the planets together. Real space is huge, and mostly empty.
Earth spins around once every day. What is that motion, and what does it make?
What gives us a whole year?
The sun is…
Which shows the first four planets, in order from the sun?
In real space, how are the planets spaced?
<soft>You know your solar system!</soft> [pause] Well done, astronomer.
Good try! Let's watch spin and travel once more.
Lesson done! Pick one planet, and go learn one amazing fact about it.
